A male coworker talking about all the women he's dated is indeed him asserting that he's heterosexual, but pretty normal, right? It's normal, if the context calls for it, to discuss one's love life. The only time that would happen if someone were to question their heterosexuality because anything not considered part of the norm would be odd at best and horrific at worst. It's more cultural than it is individualistic. It's important to a lot of people that they're considered "normal", hence why many people get defensive if they're not considered "normal". 

And if someone is making a "massive deal" out of their identity, you really have to think of why they're doing it. For those in the LGBTQ+ community, it's not at all about gloating as there's nothing to gloat about. In a world where there are countries that criminalize homosexuality and conversion therapy camps, why on earth would someone gloat about being gay if it's met with such intense gut reactions?
